sites.functional_impact_measured: Electrophysiology: tag demonstrated not to affect electrophysiological properties (DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606; Akhavan et al. 2003 cited therein). Surface trafficking: confirmed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy in HEK293T cells (PMC7704534). Processing and function: 'does not interfere with processing and function' (PMC3861077, citing Akhavan et al. 2003). On-Cell/In-Cell surface quantification confirmed (PMC13182972).
sites.rationale: The ledger provides an exact-residue citation: HA tag inserted between T443 and E444 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of full-length KCNH2. Python verification confirms seq_dict[443]='T' and seq_dict[444]='E', matching the paper's stated residues exactly. The junction sits within the extracellular span 430–453 (authoritative topology). Distance from TM1 end (residue 429): 14 aa; distance from TM2 start (residue 454): 10 aa — both well above the ≥3 aa minimum. C445 is 2 positions C-terminal to the junction and C449 is 6 positions away; these cysteines are known to form a disulfide in the turret, but the published HA tag at this exact junction was tolerated without disrupting electrophysiology, demonstrating the insert does not perturb the disulfide. Multiple independent papers confirm surface display and functional integrity. Ranked first because electrophysiology was explicitly measured and found unaffected. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A previously published 34 9 amino acid HA tag with surrounding 4 amino acid linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE) was inserted between amino acids T443 and E444 (in the extracellular region between the S1 and S2 helices) by inverse PCR 35 (Table S1).
